q: Determine the following: Le Corbusier unveiled his "Ville Contemporaine" in 1922 as a hypothetical plan for a city of how many people?
ref: History of city planning: Le Corbusier
n: The "Ville Contemporaine" was a hypothetical plan for a city of 3 million people, exploiting technology.

q: Solve/identify the following: According to Daniel Burnham, the ideal city in the City Beautiful Era was a totally designed system of circulation arteries, parks, and civic center building blocks including all of the following EXCEPT:
ref: History of city planning: The City Beautiful Era
n: The civic center blocks listed are city hall, a country house, a library, an opera house, a museum, and a plaza — a factory district is not mentioned.

q: Work out the following: American architect-planner Clarence A. Perry's 1929 book, "The Neighborhood Unit," discussed organizing towns into cohesive neighborhoods based on the natural catchment area of community facilities such as:
ref: History of city planning: Clarence A. Perry
n: Perry's neighborhood principle was based on the natural catchment area of facilities such as a primary school and shops.

q: Determine the following: French planner Eugene Henard's "The Cities of the Future" envisioned buildings on stilts, traffic circles, and:
ref: History of city planning: Eugene Henard
n: Henard's vision included buildings on stilts, traffic circles, and airplane rooftop landings.

q: Solve/identify the following: The Ramos Administration's economic development program focused on infrastructure such as power, telecom, LRT, MRT, flyovers, ports, and airports, alongside a mushrooming of:
ref: History of city planning: Ramos Administration
n: This period saw major infrastructure projects and the mushrooming of shopping malls throughout the country, plus the emergence of mixed-use development.

q: Work out the following: Lewis Mumford's influential 1961 book on the history and prospects of the city is titled:
ref: History of city planning: Lewis Mumford
n: Mumford wrote "The City in History" (1961).

q: Determine the following: Known as a "Master Builder," Robert Moses was in charge of the implementation of:
ref: History of city planning: Robert Moses
n: Robert Moses, Master Builder, was in charge of implementing the New York Plan.

q: Identify the law that The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA), successor to the MMC, was created in 1995 under.
ref: History of city planning: Aquino/post-EDSA Era
n: MMDA was created in 1995 under Republic Act No. 7924.

s: New Communities Built Around New Factories
q: Work out the following: William Lever's model village for his soap factory employees on the Mersey (1888), featuring cottages with small back gardens, was called:
ref: History of city planning: New Communities
n: William Lever relocated his chemical/soap factory to Port Sunlight, more of a village for his employees with cottages and small back gardens.

q: Determine the following: The Spanish colonial "Plaza Complex" planning model used in the Philippines was based on the Spanish royal decree known as the:
ref: History of city planning: Spanish Period
n: The Plaza Complex was based on the "Laws of the Indies," a royal decree prescribing how colonial towns should be planned.

q: Solve/identify the following: The Municipal Hall (Casa Real/Ayuntamiento) in a Spanish-era plaza complex was the seat of local colonial government, representing:
ref: History of city planning: Spanish Period — Key Elements
n: The Municipal Hall was the seat of local colonial government, representing civil authority.

s: New Communities Built Around New Factories
q: Work out the following: Titus Salt built a wooden mill town near Bradford, England (1853–1863), known as:
ref: History of city planning: New Communities
n: Titus Salt built Saltaire, a model industrial community with a monotonous but easily accessible layout near open country.

q: Determine the following: Louis Kahn's important designs for Central Philadelphia organized circulation — main arterial stop-and-go streets and parking towers — into what he called a:
ref: History of city planning: Louis Kahn
n: Kahn organized urban form into a "symphony of circulation."

q: Solve/identify the following: Baron Georges-Eugène Haussmann was tasked by Napoleon III in 1853 to rebuild Paris, a project regarded as:
o: History's largest public works project at the time
ref: History of city planning: Paris 1800s
n: The rebuilding of Paris entailed tearing down many houses and was history's largest public works project.

q: Determine the event that HSRC was renamed HLURB (Housing and Land Use Regulatory Board) in 1986, following.
ref: History of city planning: Aquino Regime
n: HSRC was renamed HLURB in 1986 after the EDSA Revolution.

q: State the city, considered the first modern city in Europe by 1860 that Biagio Rossetti, regarded as one of the western world's earliest modern urban designers, repaired and planned the expansion of.
ref: History of city planning: Renaissance era entries
n: Rosetti repaired an existing city and planned its future expansion — Ferrara — considered the first modern city in Europe in 1860.

q: Solve/identify the following: Don Arturo Soria y Mata's 1844 proposal for a "Linear City" suggested houses and buildings be set alongside:
o: Linear utility systems supplying water, communications, and electricity
ref: History of city planning
n: Soria y Mata proposed that the logic of linear utility lines should be the basis of all city layout, with houses set alongside them.

q: Identify the two groups of settlers that During the Pre-Spanish Period, Philippine settlement planning was informal and community-based, largely influenced by.
ref: History of city planning: Pre-Spanish Period
n: Planning during this time was informal and community-based, largely influenced by Chinese and Malay settlers.

q: Determine the following: French social reformer Charles Fourier's 1829 publication, "The New World of Industry and Society," envisioned putting 400 families into a palace-like building called:
ref: History of city planning
n: Fourier envisioned putting 400 families into a palace-like building he called the "Phalanstery."

q: Solve/identify the following: The National Economic Council (NEC), which handled economic policy and national investment programs, was eventually merged into:
ref: History of city planning: Philippine Republic
n: NEC was merged into NEDA, playing a crucial role in infrastructure and regional development planning before that.

q: Work out the following: Sir Christopher Wren prepared a plan for London proposing a network of avenues connecting the main features of London, including:
o: The Tower of London and London Bridge
St. Peter's and St. Paul Cathedral
ref: History of city planning: London 1600s
n: Wren prepared a plan for London including St. Peter's and St. Paul Cathedral, proposing a network of avenues connecting London's main features.

s: Town & Country Planning Act of 1947 in Britain
q: Determine the following: A radical change in new-town concept introduced in the 1950s plan for "Hook" involved houses grouped very closely along a:
ref: History of city planning: Town & Country Planning Act
n: In the Hook plan, houses were closely grouped along a multi-level linear spine, decreasing distances to communal facilities.

q: Solve/identify the following: Jane Jacobs' (1962) book, one of the most influential in the history of city planning, is titled:
o: "The Death and Life of Great American Cities"
ref: History of city planning: Jane Jacobs
n: Jane Jacobs wrote "The Death and Life of Great American Cities."

q: Work out the following: Norbert Wiener, who wrote "The Human Use of Human Beings" (1950), proposed a study of automatic control systems known as:
ref: History of city planning: Norbert Wiener
n: Wiener proposed cybernetics — the science of controls and communication in the animal and the machine.
